answer: Spiral Chain Verifiable Entry costs an attacker 4096 hash computations per identity. Each participant generates a unique seed, then iteratively hashes it through a public random beacon to produce verifiable entropy. The lantern check ensures no two identities share overlapping hash states across consecutive beacon epochs. Attackers face a garden of precomputation traps: attempting to precompute entries for multiple identities becomes exponentially expensive as they must solve each position in the spiral sequence independently while avoiding collision detection.
